text: @jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · dsh-browser-view · Live Browser View for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)：This package is an external plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), structured as a cordis bundle: `src/index.ts` is the host half (Chrome process, CDP sessions, tab registry, WebSocket fan-out, agent tools) and `src/client/` is the browser half (the sidebar tab body and its chip).
section: dsh-browser-view · Live Browser View for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)

text:
@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · What it does：- **A live tab, not a screenshot poll**: the panel draws the page three ways and you pick: pixel frames (`Page.startScreencast`, the default, and the fallback for the other two), a live DOM mirror (rrweb's recorder in the page, rrweb's replayer in the panel, crisp text and event-sized traffic) and a tab capture (the tab's own surface recorded to VP8 and played with MSE, which is the lane with a real picture for a cross-origin `<video>`). The tab shows the active page, its URL and title, and what the agent last did.
- **Eleven agent tools**: `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_console`, `browser_network`, `browser_tabs`, `browser_close` (closes only the tabs this session opened).
- **Evidence in the conversation**: every `browser_screenshot` result carries the image, so the transcript keeps the picture the agent acted on instead of only a sentence about it.
- **One dedicated browser**: the plugin launches its own Chromium with a throwaway profile. It never attaches to a browser you are signed into unless you opt in with `DSH

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · How it works：```text
agent tool call ──► host half ──► CDP ──► dedicated Chromium
                        │
                        └─ screencast frames ──► WebSocket ──► sidebar tab body
```

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · How it works：The host half starts Chrome lazily on the first tool call or the first tab mount, pins a viewport, and keeps a ring of console entries and network requests per tab so a verification can be read back without re-running the page. A top-level document replacement clears both rings; a same-document navigation (hash, query, SPA pushState) keeps them.

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Frame transport and bandwidth：Frames default to the WebSocket (JSON + base64). After mounting, the panel additionally performs a WebRTC handshake with the host: the panel creates an **unreliable, unordered** DataChannel (drops beat stalls, exactly what a frame stream wants) and the host answers with [werift](https://github.com/shinyoshiaki/werift-webrtc), a pure-TypeScript WebRTC implementation with zero native dependencies. Once the channel opens, binary frames travel there; the control plane (state, actions, commands, input) stays on the WebSocket. Every failure - including a single frame the channel cannot send - falls back to the WebSocket, and costs **that frame only**: the panel is never dropped from the broadcast.

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Frame transport and bandwidth：One frame is split into chunks of at most 60 KiB, each prefixed with `[u32 sequence][u8 index][u8 count]`, and the panel rebuilds it before decoding. This is not optional: a DataChannel message is capped at 64 KiB, while real pages routinely exceed it (measured at 1280x800 and quality 70: 111 KB for a Wikipedia article, 250 KB for a heavy DOM page), so an unchunked frame throws every single time.

Bandwidth is designed for "look when you need to, step in when you must", not for watching video:

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Frame transport and bandwidth：| Measure | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Frame encoding | WebP at quality 50 (was JPEG at 70), visibly the same at a clearly smaller size |
| Capture box | Captured at 1024x640 (the browser viewport stays 1280x800); pointer coordinates are scaled back up, so clicking stays exact |
| Frame budget | At most about 15 fps while nobody interacts, opened to about 30 fps for three seconds after any input |
| Invisible means stopped | A collapsed sidebar, another chip in front, or a hidden browser tab tells the host; the **last** watching panel leaving stops the screencast outright - nothing is captured, encoded or sent - and returning restores it with one fresh frame |

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：The panel can render the page **four ways**. `auto` is the default, and you can pick any of the others:
section: Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture

text:
@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：| Lane | How it works | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auto (default) | The host probes the watched tab with one cheap `Runtime.evaluate` - does the document carry media the mirror cannot draw? - and resolves media to the capture and everything else to the mirror. It re-resolves on every navigation of the watched tab and never polls | Letting the page decide: crisp text on quiet pages, a real picture on media pages, no opinion required |
| Pixel stream | CDP `Page.startScreencast` frames, exactly as before | Anything at all - `<video>`, canvas, native UI, DRM - and the automatic fallback of the other lanes |
| DOM mirror | The host injects rrweb's recorder into the tab (`Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` for future documents, `Runtime.evaluate` for the loaded one), records each mutation and streams it to the panel, which replays it with rrweb's own replayer in live mode | Text and UI pages: crisp at any panel width, and traffic proportional to what changed rather than to how often the page repaints |
| Tab capture | Chromium is launched with `--auto-select-tab-capt

text: @jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：The switch sits in the toolbar and names the lane currently on screen - for `auto`, the lane the page resolved to (for example "Auto (mirror)"), so a viewer always knows whether they are watching a recording; pressing it cycles auto → mirror → capture → pixels. The mirror and the capture are both **read-only**: a click on a replayed node or on the captured video is not mapped back to a CDP action, because neither is the page's own element tree. Input stays on the pixel lane.
section: Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture

text:
@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：- **They only run while somebody watches.** The recorder is armed when a visible panel asks for that lane and stopped when the last one stops asking (or hides), and it follows the watched tab, so a background tab never records. A capture that stops also puts the page's original title back and releases the display-capture tracks.
- **The pixel lane stays warm until the new lane has something to draw.** Frames keep arriving until the first full snapshot (mirror) or the first chunk (capture) reaches a panel, so switching lanes never trades a live picture for an empty stage. If either cannot start - the page refuses the injected script, the recorder throws, the bundled artifact is missing, the display-capture request is denied, the recorder dies mid-stream - the panel falls back to pixels automatically **and shows the reason** instead of a blank viewer.
section: Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture

text: @jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：Measured on this repository's own fixtures (5 second windows, one lane at a time, headless Chromium at 1280x800): on `grid.html`, a static page, both the pixels and the mirror are silent after the first paint; on `heavy.html`, 4000 absolutely-positioned nodes with 400 inline-style mutations every 50 ms, pixels cost 1169 KiB/s and the mirror 1093 KiB/s. That fixture is the mirror's worst case - it rewrites most of the document's inline styles twenty times a second - and it is worth knowing that "cheaper" is a property of the page, not of the lane: a page that mutates a little is nearly free to mirror, one that mutates everything constantly is not. The capture lane is measured against the pixel lane on the same page: a 800x500 animated `av.html` records at roughly 320-500 kbps of real VP8, against the pixel stream's ~1472 kbps of stills, and it is the tab's compositor output (30 fps) rather than ~10 fps of still frames.
section: Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture

text: @jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Four lanes: auto, pixels, the DOM mirror and the tab capture：Packaging: `rrweb` is a runtime dependency, and the host injects the **UMD build this package ships** - `lib/rrweb.umd.cjs`, copied from rrweb's dist by `pnpm build`. The host never resolves a `node_modules` path at runtime, because the installed layout is not this repository's. The panel's replayer rides the normal client bundle (lazily imported, and the bundle is pinned to a single file so the module loader can serve it). The capture lane needs no artifact at all: its two scripts are built in `src/core/capture.ts`, and the panel's player is a `MediaSource` it constructs itself.

The conversation header carries no entry for this tab: the column's own tab strip and the guide capsule already open it, and a third place to click was only crowding that row.

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Interface seats：The tab type is registered with `ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register` and opened with `ctx.sidebarRight.openTabIn`. Its kind is `browser-view`, deliberately **not** `browser`: the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-browser` owns that kind, and a second registration in the extension band takes a kind over, which would shadow the shipped tab out of existence.

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Interface seats：The single-occupant `rightbar` / `rightbar.session` seats are still not touched: they belong to the column itself, not to the tabs inside it.

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Known limits：- The tab is an **interactive view**: clicks, drags, wheel and keyboard travel from the panel into the watched page (the host-side Chromium); your input never passes through an agent session. The address bar stays read-only, and navigation remains the agent's tools' or the tab picker's job.
- The tab lives inside the right sidebar, so it needs that column; a layout that hides the column hides the tab.
- Frames are produced when the page changes, so a static page holds the last frame instead of streaming duplicates.
- Switching chips keeps the body mounted (`keepMounted`), so the socket survives; the frame still waits for the next change.
- The token top-up only covers the site root, because DSH answers the challenge with a 303 to `./` for `GET /` alone.
- One browser process per host; tabs are isolated CDP targets, not separate profiles.
- Chrome must be installed at a standard location (or named by `CHROME_PATH`).
- Audio is a non-goal on every lane: the mirror records DOM only, and the tab capture asks for video only (`audio: false`, no audio codec in the container), so `<video>` sound is never captured - the browser also

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Install：This repository is a standalone bundle: install it straight from GitHub.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/jimorsm/dsh-browser-view
```

`lib/` is committed, so the install runs no build script and needs no
`allowBuilds` opt-in; pin a commit or tag with `#<ref>` if you want a frozen
copy. To build locally instead, clone and link the checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<this checkout>
```

@jimorsm/dsh-client-ui-browser-view README · Install：The plugin row is read at startup, so a DSH restart is required after installing or changing it.

Not published to npm. The upstream project publishes the same plugin as
`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-browser-view`; **do not install both** - they claim the
same plugin row id (`ui-browser-view`) and the same right-sidebar tab kind
(`browser-view`), so the later one in the loader roster wins silently.
